## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format — tutorial metadata, pinned image
references, and a validation manifest — so that tutorials are versioned and
testable independently of Dashboard releases. This format is the shared
contract consumed both by the Dashboard's tutorial gallery (to render and
launch tutorials) and by tutorial authors (to package and validate tutorial
content).

## Scope

- Specify the tutorial metadata structure: identity, the core journey a
  tutorial covers, and the resources it expects in a user's project.
- Define how a tutorial pins the images it runs on, so a tutorial executes
  against known image versions rather than whatever is current at launch
  time.
- Define the validation manifest structure used to test a packaged tutorial
  automatically.
- Define the versioning scheme for the format itself, decoupled from
  Dashboard release versioning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The format specification documents the metadata structure, the pinned-image
  reference mechanism, and the validation manifest structure.
- A tutorial packaged per the format carries a format version that is
  independent of the Dashboard release version.
- A packaged tutorial can be checked against its validation manifest with a
  pass/fail result produced automatically.
- The format supports all six core journeys (first workbench, data prep,
  first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app),
  including both notebook-based tutorials and pipeline-based tutorials.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): tutorial packaging format — metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest; versioned and testable independently of Dashboard
  releases. (Primary coverage.)
- Indirectly enables HLR-1 (P0) and HLR-2 (P0): the gallery launch mechanics
  and the curated tutorials both build against this format, which is why this
  epic inherits P0 priority.

# Tutorial gallery and one-click launch in the Dashboard

## Description

Adds a curated tutorial gallery to the Dashboard from which a user can launch
a tutorial into their own project with one click — opening a workbench
preloaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline.
This is the product-code work stream of the tutorial gallery capability.

## Scope

- A tutorial gallery surface in the Dashboard that lists available tutorials,
  rendered from tutorial packaging metadata.
- Catalog source: packaged tutorials and their packaging metadata (including
  pinned images and the validation manifest) are published to a versioned
  tutorial catalog that the running Dashboard reads at runtime; the catalog is
  the distribution channel through which new and updated tutorials become
  visible in the gallery, updated independently of Dashboard releases (per the
  packaging format's independent versioning).
- One-click launch of a selected tutorial into the user's own project.
- Notebook tutorials launch by opening a workbench in the user's project with
  the tutorial notebook loaded, honoring the tutorial's pinned images.
- Pipeline tutorials launch by importing the pipeline into the user's
  project.
- No code changes to the workbench (Notebooks) or Data Science Pipelines
  components: launch uses their existing, GA lifecycle and import behavior.
  Correct interaction with both is validated as acceptance criteria below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user with a project and an available tutorial, when the user
  launches the tutorial from the gallery, then it opens in their project — a
  workbench with the notebook loaded for notebook tutorials, or the pipeline
  imported for pipeline tutorials.
- The gallery renders tutorials from the tutorial packaging format's
  metadata, and launches honor the pinned images each tutorial declares.
- Launching a notebook tutorial creates a workbench via the existing
  workbench lifecycle with the notebook available in it (validates the
  Notebooks component keeps working unchanged).
- Launching a pipeline tutorial results in the pipeline being available in
  the user's project via existing Data Science Pipelines behavior (validates
  the Data Science Pipelines component keeps working unchanged).
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be launched end-to-end in a test
  project without manual configuration steps beyond authentication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline).

# Six curated tutorials covering the core journeys

## Description

Authors the six curated, maintained tutorials that populate the tutorial
gallery, covering the core getting-started journeys: first workbench, data
prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, and first RAG
app. Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and tested
against the current release. This is the content-authoring work stream —
substantive authored notebook and pipeline content, distinct from the
gallery product code and from documentation.

## Scope

- Author six tutorials, one per core journey:
  1. First workbench
  2. Data prep
  3. First training run
  4. First pipeline
  5. First deployment
  6. First RAG app
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  images, and validation manifest.
- Provide a validation manifest per tutorial so each can be tested
  automatically against the current release.
- Keep the tutorials curated and maintained as the platform evolves (the
  validation manifest is the mechanism that makes re-testing repeatable).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Six tutorials exist, one for each enumerated core journey.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- Each tutorial's validation manifest passes when executed against the
  current release — every tutorial runs end-to-end successfully on the
  current release.
- Each tutorial is launchable into a fresh user project and completes its
  journey without manual fix-up steps.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): six curated tutorials covering the core journeys (first
  workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment,
  first RAG app), each tested against the current release.

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for two audiences: users who want to find and
launch tutorials, and teams who want to contribute new tutorials. This is the
documentation work stream of the tutorial gallery capability, covering usage
of the gallery and the tutorial contribution process.

## Scope

- A documentation topic covering how to use the tutorial gallery: finding a
  tutorial and launching it into your own project (notebook and pipeline
  tutorials).
- A documentation topic covering the contribution process for new tutorials:
  how a tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest) and how it is validated.
- The contribution process is documented only — no community submission
  tooling and no localization of tutorial content (both out of scope for this
  release).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery,
  including launching a notebook tutorial and a pipeline tutorial into a
  user project.
- A published documentation topic covers the contribution process for new
  tutorials, referencing the tutorial packaging format and its validation
  requirements.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and the shipped tutorials (steps and screens match actual behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials.
